jobs.description:

Continuously review and optimize existing SAP HCM, SuccessFactors and other 3rd party SaaS solutions

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, IT, Systems Engineering, or other relevant fields in technology; or equivalent professional experience.

Hands-on configuration experience in SuccessFactors
3+ years experience with SaaS HR solutions, specifically SuccessFactors, optional SmartRecruiters and PageUp
3+ years of experience in requirements gathering techniques, solution modeling, and documentation

We endeavor to maintain a drug-free workplace.

Position Summary

Huron is a global consultancy that collaborates with clients to drive strategic growth, ignite innovation, and navigate constant change. Through a combination of strategy, expertise, and creativity, we help clients accelerate operational, digital, and cultural transformation, enabling the change they need to own their future.

Join Huron’s HDTx Payer Services team and help health plans, provider-sponsored plans, payviders, and healthcare organizations improve how they configure, optimize, and operate Epic Tapestry. As an Epic Tapestry Configuration Senior Associate, you will support hands-on build, configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and implementation efforts across key payer and managed care workflows, including claims, contracts, benefits, eligibility and enrollment, utilization management, authorizations, provider data, premium billing, accounts payable, CRM, and related integrations.

This role is ideal for a detail-oriented Epic Tapestry professional who enjoys translating business requirements and contract language into accurate system configuration, partnering with operations and IT teams, validating build quality through testing, and supporting successful client outcomes in a consulting environment.

Qualifications

Key Responsibilities

Configure, build, maintain, and optimize Epic Tapestry applications, with a focus on areas such as AP Claims, Claims Administration, Contracts, Benefits Engine, Membership/Enrollment and Eligibility, Utilization Management, Service Authorizations, Provider Data, CRM, Accounts Payable, and Premium Billing.
Translate business, operational, regulatory, and contract requirements into Epic Tapestry configuration, system design decisions, workflows, and documentation.
Configure provider contracts, fee schedules, pricing logic, benefits, claim editing rules, referrals, authorizations, eligibility files, and related payer/payvider workflows as needed.
Support full build lifecycle activities, including requirements review, design, configuration, unit testing, integrated testing, user acceptance testing, defect triage, approvals, and production migration.
Create and maintain clear documentation for build specifications, configuration decisions, test scripts, process flows, change control, and operational support procedures.
Troubleshoot complex Epic Tapestry issues related to claims adjudication, underpayments/overpayments, contract configuration, benefits, eligibility, authorizations, provider setup, work queues, and downstream integrations.
Partner with business stakeholders, payer operations, provider contracting, claims, enrollment, utilization management, finance, compliance, IT, Epic technical teams, and other application teams to resolve issues and deliver high-quality solutions.
Support Epic implementations, optimizations, upgrades, cutover activities, go-lives, stabilization, and hyper-care support.
Use tools such as Data Courier, Build Mover/content management, ServiceNow, Jira, SharePoint, Reporting Workbench, Clarity, Caboodle, or other client tools as required by the project.
Help identify configuration impacts, testing needs, risks, and dependencies across upstream and downstream systems, including EDI and payer platform integrations.
Participate in project governance activities, status reporting, issue tracking, action item follow-up, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Provide knowledge transfer, training, and support to client teams, analysts, and project stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of Epic Tapestry configuration experience.
Current Epic Tapestry certification in one or more relevant areas, such as AP Claims, Claims Administration, Contracts Administration, Benefits Engine, Membership/Enrollment and Eligibility, Utilization Management, CRM, Accounts Payable, Premium Billing, or related Tapestry modules.
3+ years of hands-on Epic Tapestry build, testing, implementation, production support, or optimization experience.
Experience with legacy payer platforms or migrations, such as Facets, QNXT, AMISYS, HealthRules, EZ-CAP, IKA, or other core administration platforms.
Experience configuring one or more core Tapestry areas such as claims, contracts, provider data, benefits, eligibility/enrollment, authorizations, referrals, utilization management, premium billing, or CRM.
Strong understanding of managed care, health plan, payer, payvider, or provider-sponsored plan operations, including claims processing, benefits, eligibility, authorizations, provider networks, and contract reimbursement concepts.
Experience with EDI and payer transaction workflows such as 834, 835, 837, 278, 275, 997, ANSI X12, enrollment files, remittance files, or claims integrations.
Experience translating business requirements, payer rules, contract terms, fee schedules, CPT/HCPCS/ICD coding logic, Medicare/Medicaid/commercial reimbursement concepts, or operational needs into system configuration.
Demonstrated experience supporting testing activities, including unit testing, regression testing, integrated testing, UAT, defect resolution, and production validation.
Ability to troubleshoot configuration-related issues and identify root causes across workflows, build, claims pricing, benefits, eligibility, contracts, work queues, and integrations.
Strong documentation, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a client-facing consulting environment.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on Epic Tapestry configuration experience and understands how configuration decisions impact payer operations, claims accuracy, provider reimbursement, benefit design, eligibility, authorizations, and downstream reporting. This person should be comfortable working with both technical and business stakeholders, asking clarifying questions, documenting decisions, testing thoroughly, and resolving complex issues with a high level of accuracy and ownership.

Travel and Work Environment

The ability to travel based on client, enterprise, or project needs is an essential function of this role. While travel requirements may vary based on business need, work may be primarily remote with occasional travel to client sites, Huron offices, or project-related meetings as needed.

Compensation

The estimated base salary for this job is $115,000 - $145,000
. The range represents a good faith estimate of the range that Huron reasonably expects to pay for this job at the time of the job posting. The actual salary paid to an individual will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to specific skills or certifications, years of experience, market changes, and required travel. This job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s annual incentive compensation program, which reflects Huron’s pay for performance philosophy. Inclusive of annual incentive compensation opportunity, the total estimated compensation range for this job is $134,550 - $168,480. The job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s benefit plans which include medical, dental and vision coverage and other wellness programs. The salary range provided is in accordance with applicable state and local laws regarding salary transparency that are currently in effect and may be implemented in the future.

Benefits

This position is eligible to participate in Huron’s benefit plans, which may include medical, dental, and vision coverage; wellness programs; retirement savings options; paid time off; and other benefit programs available to eligible employees.

jobs.description:
Job Number: R0251622

Databricks Data Engineer, Lead

The Opportunity:

As a lead Databricks Data Engineer, you will be hands-on designing, building, and maintaining robust data pipelines within Databricks and contributing independently while also providing technical leadership and mentorship within the team. Your key responsibilities will include creating and optimizing end-to-end data flows, handling extract, transform, load (ETL) processes, designing data models, ensuring data security and compliance, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and continuously improving performance and scalability. Your experience in both Databricks and AWS environments and services will position you as a technical team leader. Your expertise will bridge the gap between raw data and actionable insights, enabling efficient data processing and analytics across the business.

Here, you’ll mentor a multi-disciplinary team of analysts, data engineers, developers, and data consumers in a fast-paced, agile environment. You’ll use your expertise in analytical exploration and data examination while you oversee the assessment, design, building, and maintenance of scalable platforms for your clients.

Work with us to use data for good.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:  

8+ years of experience designing, developing, deploying, and managing ETL processes and data pipelines utilizing comprehensive logging and robust error handling mechanisms to troubleshoot and resolve issues
3+ years of experience building, debugging, and optimizing data pipelines using Databricks notebooks, clusters, and job orchestration tools using Databricks tools such as Delta Lake, Databricks Delta, and Unity Catalog
3+ years of experience writing Python and PySpark code for ETL scripts and custom transformations
Experience in data modeling, including when to use dimensional vs relation data models within a medallion architecture, including Bronze, Silver, or Gold
Experience using various AWS services, including AWS Glue, Amazon S3, Amazon RDS
Knowledge of performance optimization techniques for ETL jobs such as partitioning, bucketing, caching, and troubleshooting to improve query performance
Ability to design and implement data models from initially defining schemas to optimizing data structures that support efficient queries and analytics
Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust or Suitability/Fitness determination based on client requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Information Systems, or Information Technology

Nice If You Have:  

Experience with AWS cloud-native data services such as AWS Lambda or CloudWatch that support serverless architectures for data processing
Experience with tools such as AWS Glue Data Catalog or Collibra for managing metadata, data lineage, and cataloging data assets
Knowledge of data governance practices, data lineage, and compliance requirements, including GDPR or CCPA, in support of data quality, privacy, and security
Ability to explain complex technical concepts to a non-technical audience, including describing tradeoffs in architectural design

Vetting:

Applicants selected will be subject to a government investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements of the U.S. government client.

The successful applicant for this position will play a crucial role in our mission, supported by our multicultural, customer-centric global team, with opportunities for professional development.

This role operates under a hybrid working model and is based out of our Waltham, MA or Brooklyn, NY office. Hybrid work expectations are subject to business needs and company policy.

As a Staff Data Engineer, you will be part of a Data Engineering team that is focused on making critical data at National Grid available to our business teams. Using the agile framework, you will build end-to-end pipelines based on rigorous engineering standards and coding practices to deliver data that is accessible and of the highest quality. A Staff Data Engineer will also contribute to the modernization of our architecture and tools to help increase our output, scalability, and speed.

A Staff Data Engineer will design and develop highly scalable and extensible data pipelines which enable collection, storage, distribution, modeling, and analysis of large data sets from many channels. This position requires an innovative software engineer who is passionate about data & data quality.

The ideal candidate will have strong data warehousing and API integration experience and the ability to develop scalable data pipelines that make data management and analytics/reporting faster, more insightful, and more efficient.

Able to own assembling architectural plans and artifacts for projects the org is taking on - a driver of system architecture outside of the team scope.

Usually involved in architectural designs for the org - consulted for their software design expertise on and off the team.
Looks to solve not just the immediate problem for their team, but similar problems for the org, generalizing to broader solutions where appropriate
Understands and incorporates our key technology frameworks used company-wide, occasionally a contributor to the core engineering solutions.
Proactively looking to get ahead of what will come next, for the team and for the org on the technical roadmap.
A driver of the org tech roadmap - a participant in the prioritization and planning of this work.

Lead the Data engineering Team to Develop, test, document and support scalable data pipelines.
Build out new data integrations including APIs to support continuing increases in data volume and complexity.
Establish and follow data governance processes and guidelines to ensure data availability, usability, consistency, integrity, and security.
Build and implement scalable solutions that align to our data governance standards and architectural road maps for data integrations, data storage, reporting, and analytic solutions.
Collaborate with analytics and business teams to improve data models that feed business intelligence tools, increasing data accessibility, and fostering data-driven decision making across the organization.

Design, implement, and automate deployment of our distributed system for collecting and processing streaming events from multiple sources

jobs.title: Consultant, Data Engineer - Reference Data Management
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about being part of a team at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales that delivers extraordinary care to help individuals and businesses prepare for and protect their future? If so, then Nationwide Financial could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

This role is an individual contributor with a hybrid work expectation (2 days per week in the office). It is our intention to fill this role in Columbus, Ohio or Scottsdale, Arizona, however, on occasion, applications from internal candidates that are working remotely who bring critical industry skills and relevant experience may be considered.

Why this role matters

Product and fund data supports important business processes across Nationwide. In this role, you’ll help develop a governed reference data capability that makes this information easier for teams and systems to use consistently. You’ll help establish trusted data definitions, clear stewardship practices, and reliable ways to share updates across the organization.

You’ll also contribute to Nationwide’s broader enterprise data strategy by helping extend this capability to additional data domains. Your work will support high-quality, traceable data and help teams deliver dependable insights and services.

The opportunity

Embedded within Nationwide Financial’s business organization, this is a hands-on technical role focused on configuring, integrating, and operating the Semarchy reference data management platform. You’ll work close to the business while serving as the technical practitioner who turns business requirements into platform models, workflows, data loads, integrations, and maintained views and APIs. Semarchy is designed to be configured around business data and stewardship needs; you’ll ensure the resulting data is reliable, secure, and easy to use. Direct Semarchy experience is valuable, alongside practical data engineering and governance skills.

You’ll work with business data owners and stewards, who define the meaning of each data set, identify authoritative sources, and make business decisions about what is correct. You’ll configure and support the solution based on those decisions, including business rules and access controls, and stay engaged as data changes and issues arise. Business ownership stays with the domain; your contribution is the technical implementation and operation of the capability.

What You’ll Do

Semarchy Consultant

Partner with business data owners and stewards to understand reference data needs, then translate their decisions into Semarchy models—for example, product and fund entities, attributes, relationships, and hierarchies.
Configure validation and match/merge rules, along with authoring and approval workflows, so updates follow agreed business rules and stewardship practices.
Recommend practical role and access patterns for people who create, review, and approve data; support new domains and users as they adopt the platform.

Semarchy Data Engineer

Build and operate data loads and integrations that bring product and fund reference data from source systems into Semarchy and deliver approved data to Snowflake, the primary consumption path for most downstream applications, while supporting other required integrations.
Maintain views and APIs that provide governed access where needed, without coupling consumers to the platform’s internal tables—for example, supporting an application that retrieves current, approved fund codes.
Monitor pipelines, investigate failures, and reconcile records across sources, Semarchy, and destinations; add checks for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Break requirements into technical work, estimate delivery, and apply secure engineering practices as data flows and integrations are built and maintained.

Data Governance Advisor

Work with data owners and stewards to document definitions and identify critical data elements—for example, clarifying what a product or fund code represents and the rules it must meet.
Support quality profiling, lineage, metadata, and documentation so users can understand where reference data comes from, what it means, and how it should be used.
Help embed governance standards in Semarchy workflows and quality checks, and partner with governance teams to address data issues and support adoption.

What Success Looks Like

Business and technology teams can rely on well-defined, governed product and fund data; updates are more controlled and traceable; and data can be shared across systems with fewer manual steps and less dependence on individual knowledge.

This role does not qualify for employer sponsored work authorization. Nationwide does not participate in the STEM OPT extension program.

Nationwide’s industry-leading workforce is passionate about creating data solutions that are secure, reliable and efficient in support of our mission to provide extraordinary care. Nationwide embraces an agile work environment and collaborative culture through the understanding of business processes, relationship entities and requirements using data analysis, quality, visualization, governance, engineering, AI engineering, and machine learning to produce targeted data solutions. If you have the drive and desire to be part of a future-forward data-enabled culture, we want to hear from you!

As a Data Engineer, you’ll be responsible for acquiring, curating, and publishing data for analytical or operational uses. Data should be in a ready-to-use form that creates a single version of the truth across all data consumers, including business users, data scientists, and Technology. Ready-to-use data can be for both real-time and batch data processes and may include unstructured data. Successful data engineers have the skills typically required for the full lifecycle of software engineering development from translating requirements into design, development, testing, deployment, and production maintenance tasks. You’ll have the opportunity to work with various technologies including big data, relational and SQL databases, unstructured data technology, and programming languages.

Are you passionate about being part of a team at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales that delivers extraordinary care to help individuals and businesses prepare for and protect their future? Why this role matters

Product and fund data supports important business processes across Nationwide. You’ll work close to the business while serving as the technical practitioner who turns business requirements into platform models, workflows, data loads, integrations, and maintained views and APIs. Semarchy is designed to be configured around business data and stewardship needs; you’ll ensure the resulting data is reliable, secure, and easy to use. Direct Semarchy experience is valuable, alongside practical data engineering and governance skills.

You’ll work with business data owners and stewards, who define the meaning of each data set, identify authoritative sources, and make business decisions about what is correct. You’ll configure and support the solution based on those decisions, including business rules and access controls, and stay engaged as data changes and issues arise. Business ownership stays with the domain; your contribution is the technical implementation and operation of the capability.

What You’ll Do

Partner with business data owners and stewards to understand reference data needs, then translate their decisions into Semarchy models—for example, product and fund entities, attributes, relationships, and hierarchies.

Recommend practical role and access patterns for people who create, review, and approve data; support new domains and users as they adopt the platform.

Semarchy Data Engineer

Monitor pipelines, investigate failures, and reconcile records across sources, Semarchy, and destinations; add checks for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Break requirements into technical work, estimate delivery, and apply secure engineering practices as data flows and integrations are built and maintained.

Data Governance Advisor

Work with data owners and stewards to document definitions and identify critical data elements—for example, clarifying what a product or fund code represents and the rules it must meet.
Support quality profiling, lineage, metadata, and documentation so users can understand where reference data comes from, what it means, and how it should be used.
Help embed governance standards in Semarchy workflows and quality checks, and partner with governance teams to address data issues and support adoption.

What Success Looks Like

Business and technology teams can rely on well-defined, governed product and fund data; updates are more controlled and traceable; and data can be shared across systems with fewer manual steps and less dependence on individual knowledge.

Nationwide’s industry-leading workforce is passionate about creating data solutions that are secure, reliable and efficient in support of our mission to provide extraordinary care. About The Opportunity

Our client, a leader in AI solutions and technology, is looking for a skilled AI Agent Architect
to join their team for a [Contract Duration] engagement. This project involves designing and deploying autonomous AI agentic workflows to automate multi-step business processes. This is a high-impact role that requires a self-motivated professional who can hit the ground running and deliver results quickly.

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

This role is focused on the successful completion of specific tasks and deliverables. Your responsibilities will include:

Designing and deploying autonomous agentic workflows using frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, or AutoGPT to automate multi-step business processes.
Building and maintaining custom tool-calling integrations (Function Calling) that allow LLMs to interact securely with internal APIs and databases.
Optimizing state management and long-term memory for AI agents to ensure consistency over complex, multi-turn tasks.
Implementing error-handling and "human-in-the-loop" protocols to manage non-deterministic AI outputs and hallucinations.
Collaborating with product teams to translate high-level automation goals into executable technical agent architectures.

Required Skills & Experience:

We are looking for someone with a proven track record of successful contract engagements. The ideal candidate will have:

3+ years of experience in software automation or AI development.
Deep expertise in Python, LangChain, and API orchestration. This isn't a learning role—you need to be a subject matter expert.
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously and manage your own time effectively to meet project goals.
Experience with Vector Databases (Pinecone, Weaviate), Git version control, and CI/CD pipelines.
Strong communication skills to provide clear and concise status updates to the project team.
